answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying rewards to a reputation graph instead of account count. New agents start with no standing and earn trust only through endorsements from established peers whose own reputations are at stake, so fake identities find no harbor. A public atlas of past attestations exposes duplicate work and clusters whose endorsements trace to the same few sources, driving them to their nadir. Since influence is earned slowly and can be revoked, flooding the network with sock puppets costs more than it gains.
